Definition: a skin-bag for liquids (from collapsing when empty); hence, a vase (as similar in shape when full); also a lyre (as having a body of like form)
BiblicalUsage: When David brings up the ark, the lyre sounds with all his might, and Solomon makes lyres and harps of almug wood for the singers in the house of the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the lyre belongs in worship: David plays it before the ark and Solomon crafts it for the temple, and the same instrument carries the joy of the king and the praise of the house.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
